info.name: Ecommerce Mobile App API AtmaNirbhar
info.description:
Mobile-app-only API surface for this Rails app (app/controllers/api/v1/mobile/**, routed under /api/v1/mobile in config/routes.rb).

Excludes the admin/web dashboard, franchise, affiliate and customer-web-portal controllers — this collection is scoped strictly to what the mobile app calls.

Insurance-related mobile endpoints (customer insurance portfolio, agent dashboard/leads/commission, insurance-derived login stats) have been removed from the mobile API entirely — those features remain in the app's admin/web side but are no longer exposed to the mobile app.

## Auth model
One shared JWT login endpoint (Authentication > Login) serves four different account types — Customer, User(agent/sub_agent), SubAgent, DeliveryPerson — differentiated by `data.role` in the response. Send the token back as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (30-day expiry, HS256, signed with Rails.application.secret_key_base).

Because a mobile device is usually only ever ONE of these roles at a time, this collection saves the token into 4 collection variables after every login:
- `token` — always set to whatever the last login returned
- `customer_token` — set when data.role == 'customer'
- `agent_token` — set when data.role == 'agent' or 'sub_agent'
- `delivery_token` — set when data.role == 'delivery_person'

Agent/sub-agent accounts can still log in and use Settings (profile, password, terms, contact, helpdesk) — the dedicated agent dashboard/leads/commission endpoints and insurance-derived login stats have been removed.

## base_url
Defaults to the production host found hardcoded in app/controllers/api/v1/mobile/authentication_controller.rb — change the `base_url` collection variable to point at localhost or staging.

item.name: 1. Authentication
item.description: Shared authentication endpoints used by every mobile role. Run 'Login' first — its test script populates {{token}} for the rest of the collection.

request.description:
Single login endpoint shared by every mobile role. The backend tries, in order: User (agent/admin/customer login), Customer, DeliveryPerson, SubAgent. `username` accepts an email OR a 10-digit Indian mobile number (also accepts +91/91-prefixed variants). Response `data.role` tells you which type of account logged in (customer | agent | sub_agent | delivery_person) and `data.token` is a 30-day JWT to send as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

A test script on this request auto-saves the token into {{token}} and into the role-specific variable ({{customer_token}} / {{agent_token}} / {{delivery_token}}) so the rest of the collection works without manual copy/paste.

Creates both a Customer record and a linked User (for login) inside a DB transaction. Requires: first_name, last_name, email, mobile, password. Mobile must be a valid 10-digit Indian number (6-9 start). Fails 409 if email/mobile already used, 422 on validation errors.
Creates a User with user_type=agent, role=agent_role and status=false (pending admin approval - cannot log in until an admin activates the account).

Looks up the account across User, Customer and SubAgent by email or mobile. NOTE: current implementation only generates a reset token in memory and does not actually persist it or send an email yet - it always returns a generic success message when the account is found.
